title: Service-class shedder: graded degradation + admission control for multi-tenant inference
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Design and implement a service-class oriented load-shedding subsystem ("Service-class shedder") for the Redwood runtime that combines admission control,
priority-weighted token buckets, and graded degradation modes. The goal is to protect
SLOs for high-value interactive workloads while allowing best-effort background and lower-tier
traffic to be stepped down gracefully during overload or partial region outages.
summary:
Build a runtime component that classifies requests into service-classes and enforces
admission policies with multiple degradation strategies (partial response, skeleton, cached
reply, model-quantize fallback, and controlled 429/503) plus observability and canary rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can tag incoming requests with service_class metadata (prod:interactive, prod:background, tiered-customer:X)
Admission controller implements weighted token-bucket per-service-class with dynamic target rates from Console
At overload, at least three graded degradation strategies available and selectable by policy: token-limit, prefix-cache, fast-light-model-fallback
Circuit-breakers per-region detect 30s sustained elevated p95 latency or >15% error rate and trigger regional shedder fallback within 60s
Metric coverage: per-class rejection rate, average tokens served per request, degrade-mode distribution, SLO violation attribution
Canary rollout to 10% host pool in us-west2 without regressions in existing production traffic (rollback plan exists)
Automated e2e chaos test that injects 40% QPS spike and verifies overall p99 latency for interactive class remains within SLOs 95% of trials
design_notes:
Key concepts and trade-offs:

1) Service-class model: classify by {customer_tier, route_type (chat/generate/embeddings), latency_sensitivity}.
   Rationale: priorities must reflect business value; single global queue won't preserve SLO for premium interactive flows.

2) Admission control: implement per-class token buckets where token rate is a function of configured SLO targets and real-time health signals.
   Trade-off: strict admission keeps p99 low but increases tail rejections; choose conservative target to avoid cascading retries.

3) Graded degradation modes (ordered by fidelity):
   - Full: normal model execution.
   - Model-fallback: switch to cheaper, quantized variant (smaller context) with affinity-aware routing.
   - Cached-skeleton: serve cached prefix and mark response as partial with metadata.
   - Token-trim: cap max tokens returned and add explanation header.
   - Reject-with-retry-after: short 429 with estimated retry window.

4) Observability: classify SLI attribution so we can answer "which class caused this SLO miss" and run per-class burn-down.
5) Multi-region behavior: prefer local shedding first; if region-level circuit-breaker trips, route to healthy region or fallback model depending on cost/latency budget.

Decision: implement admission + graded fallback as interfaces in runtime to allow per-customer policy overrides; keep default global policies in Console.
implementation_notes: Add service_class header to internal ingress (ingest-layer) and propagate in tracing spans
New shedder component inside request router: evaluates admission before queueing to executor
Token-bucket implementation uses shared leaky-bucket store with local soft-reservations for low-latency checks (Redis for cross-host aggregation)
Fallback adapters: model-fallback (route to quantized endpoint), cache-adapter (prefix cache lookup), and synthetic-409 adapter (structured partial reply)
Config surface: per-class target_qps, max_concurrency, degrade_order, cost_weight, retry_budget
Runtime hooks: on_reject, on_degrade, on_fallback with telemetry emission and optional synthetic-headers for callers
Backpressure signal to API gateway: emit X-Redwood-Shedder-Reason and Retry-After when rejecting
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: internal-only feature flag rollout to k8s canary pool (10%). Verify metrics and no new latency regressions.
Phase 2: enable for 5 low-risk customers (beta), monitor console dashboards and run explicit load tests.
Phase 3: enable default policies globally with conservative thresholds; enable per-customer opt-out.
Rollback: instant feature-flag disable and dynamic draining of shedder queues; post-mortem triggers if >3% additional errors after rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket math and degrade-order evaluation
Integration tests: simulated mixed traffic (50% interactive, 30% background, 20% batch) verifying per-class SLIs under synthetic pressure
Chaos test: kill regional endpoint, verify circuit-breaker opens and fallback routing works within configured windows
Load test: spike QPS to 3x normal and assert interactive class p99 < SLO threshold in >=95% runs
E2E canary smoke: verify headers emitted, traces have shedder spans, and client SDK surfaces structured fallback reasons
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-class QPS, tokens_consumed, rejections, degrade_mode_breakdown
Alerts: per-class rejection_rate > 1% sustained for 5m, per-region circuit-breaker open > 60s
SLO incident enrichment: add shedder attribution to SLO alert payloads
Automated rollback alert: if canary shows >2x error rate vs baseline, auto-disable flag
